answer.summary: Johari says leaders should expect data scientists to explain what experiments teach about the business—not just report statistically rigorous results or declare winners and losers.

sections.heading: Contribute business learning
sections.content: Leaders should expect data scientists to share what they are learning about the business through their work, including insights that can inform creative and strategic business change—not only deliver narrowly defined statistical results.

sections.heading: Make experiments hypothesis-driven
sections.content: Experiments should be framed around what they can teach, not only whether they win or lose. Johari suggests stating the hypotheses in an experiment or launch document and asking what a test will reveal about a business flow, funnel, guest or host preferences, or demand elasticity when prices change.
